subject: derived occupancy (psi) and detectability (p) from occuRN rather than N and r

messages.author: e187aa8cf27d2634
messages.subject: derived occupancy (psi) and detectability (p) from occuRN rather than N and r
parts:
Hi folks!

 I have two questions, one specific and other more general.

 I have a Royle-Nichols model from detection- non-detection data fitted with occuRN from unmarked. I assume that I'm obtaining abundance estimates when using predict( type="state") since values are > 0 (which makes sense since the model is parametrized on N and r rather than Psi and p). Following Chapter 7 from the book of MacKenzie et al "Occupancy estimation and modeling" I understand that both, occupancy (psi) and detectability (p) are derived parameters that could be estimated (given the abundance Poisson model, for example). is there any function in unmarked package to obtain this parameters directly? I'd like to compare the outputs from occu with occuRN, and I think it would be better to compare them in terms of psi and p... isn't it?

 Another more general question, I'd like to fit a multi-season  Royle-Nichols model like in Rossman et al. 2016 (Ecology 97: 3300-3307) but controlling by spatial autocorrelation in response (iCAR, SAR or whatever available). I think that this is only available through Bayesian inference. I have some knowledge in STAN, but I thing there are more examples for site-occupancy models in JAGS, WinBUGS. Other people recommend nimble. Do you have any advice and/or tutorial about what should I use?

 Thanks in advance

Javi
